sentences.text: Eagle Ranch Academy is a licensed residential treatment center for teenagers at 115 West 1470 South in St. George, Utah, with room for 57 young people.

sources.cite: Utah Office of Licensing inspection checklist, Aug. 14, 2025

sentences.text: It was founded by the brothers Paul and David Arslanian, former Utah State University football coaches.

sources.cite: Woodbury Reports, Dec. 2013
Deseret News, Oct. 9, 2000

sentences.text: Police logged calls to the academy reporting assaults, child abuse and runaways from 2006 on, and former students and parents have published accounts of the program since 2013 (see Survivor testimony below).

sources.cite: St. George Police Department, "LAW Incident Table by Nature," incidents at 115 W 1470 S (Eagle Ranch Academy), 2006–2013, printed Mar. 24, 2014 (KOP copy of the record HEAL posted, from the Wayback Machine capture of Apr. 27, 2016: web.archive.org/web/20160427122820/http://www.heal-online.org/erapolicecalls06thru13.pdf)
WWASP Survivors: Eagle Ranch Academy (comments by former students and parents, 2013 on)
Parent review on Yelp, Jan. 13, 2020
Parent review on Google, 2018

sentences.text: David Arslanian was Utah State's head football coach in 1998 and 1999.

sources.cite: Deseret News, Oct. 9, 2000

sentences.text: He hired his brother Paul as a coordinator over the university president's objection, was fired on December 2, 1999, and sued the university in 2000.

sources.cite: Deseret News, Oct. 9, 2000

sentences.text: By 2013 Woodbury Reports, an industry newsletter, listed David as the academy's co-founder and director of admissions.

sources.cite: Woodbury Reports, Dec. 2013

sentences.text: Paul Arslanian was the person on site when state licensers inspected the program in August 2025.

sources.cite: Utah Office of Licensing inspection checklist, Aug. 14, 2025

sentences.text: Woodbury Reports listed 1995 as the program's start year.

sources.cite: Woodbury Reports, Dec. 2013

sentences.text: In 2005 the program sought land-use permits in two southern Utah counties.

sources.cite: Washington County Planning Commission, meeting minutes, Apr. 26, 2005
Beaver County Commission, meeting minutes, May 2005

sentences.text: Seven years earlier the Salt Lake Tribune had reported that Hyrum Smith, the founder of Franklin Quest, owned the D.I. Ranch, an 831-acre cattle ranch 25 miles west of St. George, and planned to sell it to investors who wanted to turn it into a wilderness retreat for troubled youths.

sources.cite: The Salt Lake Tribune, "Utah's Rancho Bizarro," May 5, 1998

sentences.text: On April 26, 2005, the Washington County Planning Commission took up a request to run a residential treatment facility and school for 20 youths at "Eagle Ranch Academy, Inc. (a.k.a. DI Ranch)," with Dave Arslanian as one of the applicant's agents.

sources.cite: Washington County Planning Commission, meeting minutes, Apr. 26, 2005

sentences.text: The commission's chairman said the applicants were not prepared and needed to provide much more information, and the request was tabled.

sources.cite: Washington County Planning Commission, meeting minutes, Apr. 26, 2005

sentences.text: In May 2005 the Beaver County Commission, after hearing Dave Arslanian, unanimously upheld its planning commission's denial of a permit for the academy in the county's "grove" area.

sources.cite: Beaver County Commission, meeting minutes, May 2005

sentences.text: On June 7, 2005, the Washington County Commission approved the D.I. Ranch permit for 20 youths or fewer, on the applicant's statements that each youth would stay six to ten months and that no adjudicated youth would be admitted.

sources.cite: Washington County Commission, meeting minutes, June 7, 2005

sentences.text: The St. George Area Chamber of Commerce later listed Doug Caputo as the contact for D.I. Ranch LLC, also known as Kayenta Homes & Properties.

sources.cite: St. George Area Chamber of Commerce, member listing for D.I. Ranch LLC / Kayenta Homes

sentences.text: The academy's 2009 enrollment packet told parents it was licensed by the Utah Department of Human Services.

sources.cite: Eagle Ranch Academy, Inc., Admissions / Enrollment Information (enrollment packet), 2009, pp. 6–8

sentences.text: It bound families to a minimum stay of six months while reserving the program's right to dismiss a student at any time, and it authorized staff to restrain students with Positive Control Systems techniques.

sources.cite: Eagle Ranch Academy, Inc., Admissions / Enrollment Information (enrollment packet), 2009, pp. 6–8

sentences.text: The program has publicly denied any association with WWASP.

sources.cite: Eagle Ranch Academy, "ERA's Response to Hate Groups"

sentences.text: In March 2024 an investigation substantiated that staff had left clients unsupervised for longer than 15 minutes, during which they engaged in unsafe behaviors, a repeat violation.

sources.cite: Utah Office of Licensing, Eagle Ranch Academy complaint investigation, Mar. 6, 2024

sentences.text: That May licensers found the program had not reported a May 4 critical incident until May 7, also a repeat violation.

sources.cite: Utah Office of Licensing, Eagle Ranch Academy inspection, May 7, 2024

sentences.text: On November 17, 2025, an investigation found it out of compliance with the rules requiring providers to protect clients from abuse and to follow safe practices.

sources.cite: Utah Office of Licensing, Eagle Ranch Academy investigation inspection, Nov. 17, 2025

testimony.text: If you think taking away shoes and socks making kids walk on hot pavement to eat every meal to where me and others had blister on our feet is right. Or letting kids sleep in a bed with no sheets and no pillows for months is helping kids learn the ways of life? … After I was abused and dumb at ERA for the first 3 months I had no contact with anyone in my family, parents or friends. … If you think it's right to isolate kids in room alone for days or "ghost" kids for months with no contact to anyone but staff. Or that it's right to restrain kid to the ground till their rest and arms bleed, tackle and pressure point 12 to 17 year old children till they eat what you want them to eat or walk where you want them to.

I would be denied the right to talk to my parents in the beginning AND EVEN WEAR SHOES! … I remember at one point in my stay I was made to stand up in front of a room full of people and be verbally dismantled, being told I don't love my family and I was selfish and a brat for my choices I had made in the past. … I stood in front of about 20 people and cried for hours. (This was part of one of their seminars.) … While I was there I was put on various medications including anti-psychotics and anti-depressants. Medications I had no choice in taking.

Our daughter was assaulted her first day there and then restrained by an adult male that drug her in a neck hold down the hall and placed her face down on a FILTHY floor. My husband watched the video with the police and it was clear our daughter wasn't the aggressor. She also slept on that filthy dirty floor for 14 days.
ERA falsely claims they are accredited by the SAIS and SACSCOC on their home page. I have spoken to both agencies and confirmed ERA is not accredited by either.
